selectionRule: Choose the lowest selection-period log loss on identical fixtures; break numerical ties by Brier, then deterministic candidate order. Persist this choice before computing audit and monitoring metrics. Never reselect using either later period.
informationFence: For each forecast, exclude all matches on or after the day immediately before its kickoff date; fit and Elo use the same conservative UTC date fence. Filter source observations strictly before as-of minus one day.
auditGate: Both Brier and log loss improve over v1, the league-frequency baseline and the transferred EPL recipe in both audit and monitoring; both audit paired UTC-day bootstrap interval upper bounds versus v1 must be below zero.
sourcePolicy: Football-Data.co.uk E1 regular-season results only; validate division, season, identities, final regulation scores and complete closed-season counts. No odds, target-match shots, corners or cards become predictors. Do not mix the separate football-data.org frozen input files or playoff fixtures into this training source.
limitations: Retrospective development: recent ELC periods were inspected in the previous four-league experiment; no historical period is claimed to be an untouched prospective test.
CSV dates lack reliable publication timestamps, so the immediately preceding calendar day is conservatively excluded.

The CSV v1 reference uses the same past-only date fence as the candidate. It is a dated replay of the production formula, not the original one-hundred-match packet or exactly the timestamp-based online calculation.
Model settings are selected on earlier ELC seasons only. Earlier evaluation results can subsequently train later rolling forecasts once they cross the information fence.
Promoted teams may have little same-division history; primary comparisons include only fixtures eligible for v1, with exclusions and team-history coverage reported.
Only goals and prior results are used; dated injuries, lineups and xG are not supplied by this archive.
A historical improvement requires a separate future frozen comparison before changing the public model. Original one-hundred-match probabilities remain immutable.
